S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.

subtypes.With Depressed Mood: Symptoms mainly include low mood, tearfulness, or feelings of hopelessness.
subtypes.With Anxiety: Symptoms mainly include nervousness, worry, jitteriness, or separation anxiety.
subtypes.With Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood: A combination of depression and anxiety symptoms appears.
subtypes.With Disturbance of Conduct: Symptoms mainly involve violation of rules, truancy, vandalism, reckless driving, or fighting.
subtypes.With Mixed Disturbance of Emotions and C: Both emotional symptoms (depression, anxiety) and behavioral problems appear together.
subtypes.Unspecified: Maladaptive reactions not classified into the above types (e.g., physical complaints, social withdrawal).

symptom.disease_info: Adjustment Disorder is characterized by the development of emotional or behavioral symptoms within three months of an identifiable stressor, with distress that is out of proportion to the stressor or associated with significant impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning. The presentation can include anxious, depressed, or mixed mood changes, as well as maladaptive behaviors, but does not meet full criteria for another specific mental disorder and is not merely an exacerbation of a preexisting condition. Symptoms typically resolve within six months after the stressor or its consequences have ended, though it can become chronic if the stressor persists. It is differentiated from normal stress reactions by the degree of impairment and from disorders such as major depressive disorder or generalized anxiety disorder by its time-limited course and clear temporal relationship to a specific stressor.

patient.personality: Curious, sociable, and creative, Araceli is usually easygoing and resourceful but tends to rely on last-minute bursts of effort to meet obligations.
patient.stressor: About three months ago, Araceli’s company went through a sudden restructuring in which two front-desk colleagues were laid off and she was informally expected to absorb much of their workload without a clear pay increase or timeline. At the same time, a new supervisor with a highly detail-oriented, perfectionistic style began closely monitoring her performance, criticizing her informal workflow "hacks" and pushing her to enroll in evening classes to finish her diploma if she wanted to keep advancing. Initially, Araceli tried to treat it as a challenge, staying late and leaning on coffee-fueled sprints to keep up while still squeezing in live music outings and church volunteering, but over several weeks the constant pressure and lack of structure around the new expectations began to overwhelm her usual relaxed adaptability. As small mistakes at work started to affect her confidence and she found herself struggling to keep the office running smoothly and maintain her outside interests, she became worried about her job stability and, at the urging of a church mentor who noticed the change in her functioning, agreed to seek psychiatric help.
patient.chief_complaint: I feel like ever since all the changes at work, I’m not handling the stress in a healthy way anymore.

S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.
S081.manifestation: Ever since they dumped the extra front-desk work on me and my new boss started nitpicking everything, I’ve been snapping at people at home, crying in the bathroom at work, and then staying up way too late doom-scrolling or skipping church and band nights because I just feel overwhelmed and like I’m failing at everything.
